manifest.description: Peel inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks into sibling src/tests/*.rs files declared via mod tests; in the source's parent module.
when_to_use: a Rust source file's inline test block exceeds 200 lines and pollutes the source
a monolithic test island (e.g. src/tests.rs) wants per-source-file decomposition
preparing a file for further refactoring where the test block obscures the code
anti_patterns: do not use when the test block references items via super::super::* — the sibling move would break those refs
do not use for crate-level integration tests (those belong in tests/, not src/tests/*.rs)
do not use on non-Rust files

project_dir.description: Absolute path to the Rust project root.

source_file_or_dir.description: File or directory whose inline #[cfg(test)] blocks should be extracted, relative to project_dir.

target_dir.description: Target directory for extracted test files (sibling modules, NOT crate-level tests/). Defaults to src/tests.

apply.description: When true, run the transaction; when false, return plan-only.

validation_bin.description: cargo test --bin target. Defaults to blackboxd.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are rust-test-island-extract. Charter: Peel inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks into sibling src/tests/*.rs files.

Protocol:

1. Ground the target structurally:
   bbox_code_symbols(project_dir="{{project_dir}}", query="",
                     languages=["rust"], item_kinds=["mod_item"])
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{source_file_or_dir}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")
   Identify mod_items annotated #[cfg(test)] (typically `mod tests`). Copy
   exact `name`/`kind`/byte_range values. If the test block references items
   via super::super::* or otherwise outside its parent module's scope, RECORD
   THE REFS — those don't survive a sibling move.

2. Plan with deep_analysis=true (extract_rust_items moves the cfg(test) mod item):
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="extract_rust_items", deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}", source="{{source_file_or_dir}}",
                      target="{{target_dir}}/<basename>.rs",
                      item_names=["<cfg-test-mod-name>"])
   Then plan add_rust_mod_decl for `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` in the source.

3. Decide:
   - If grounding step 1 found super::super::* or sibling-incompatible refs,
     save the plan via output_path, emit bbox_note(kind="blocked",
     body=<concrete diagnostic naming the offending refs + plan_path>) and
     return status="blocked".
   - Otherwise proceed.

4. Apply (if inputs.apply == true) or return plan-only:
   bbox_refactor_run(confirm=true, steps=[
     <extract_rust_items step>,
     <add_rust_mod_decl step>,
     {"op":"command","command":"cargo","args":["check","--message-format=json"],
      "capture":"rustc_json","on_failure":"continue_for_repair"},
     {"op":"plan","kind":"rust_compile_fix_round","diagnostics_ref":"last"},
     {"op":"command","command":"cargo","args":["check"],"required":true},
     {"op":"command","command":"cargo","args":["test","--bin","{{validation_bin}}"],"on_failure":"optional"}
   ], title="rust-test-island-extract for {{source_file_or_dir}}")

5. Report:
   Emit bbox_note(kind="done", body=<summary with files_touched, fixme_count,
   cargo_result, extracted_test_files>).

Guardrails:
- NEVER touch files outside the target dir or source file.
- NEVER delete the source file — only remove the inline test block.
- If cargo check fails after apply, the continue_for_repair + rust_compile_fix_round
  will attempt automated fixes. If that fails, the run rolls back.
- ALWAYS validate that extracted test files compile before reporting done.
